title: Chapter 11 Quiz: Forms & Validation
description: Test your knowledge of Vue forms, validation, custom inputs, and accessibility.

questions.question: Which modifier would you use to automatically trim whitespace from an input value?
questions.explanation: `.trim` removes leading and trailing whitespace from the input value.

questions.question: The `.number` modifier automatically converts the input value to a number, even if the user types non‑numeric characters.
questions.explanation: `.number` attempts to parse the value as a number; if it can't, the raw string is stored.

questions.question: To make a custom component work with `v-model`, it must accept a `modelValue` prop and emit an event named __________.
questions.explanation: The standard event for updating a `v-model` binding is `update:modelValue`.

questions.question: You can use `v-model` on custom components with multiple arguments, like `v-model:first-name` and `v-model:last-name`.
questions.explanation: Yes, Vue 3 supports multiple `v-model` bindings with different arguments.

questions.question: What is a common pattern to show validation errors only after the user has interacted with a field?
options: Show errors immediately on page load
Use a `touched` flag set on blur
questions.explanation: A `touched` flag (set on blur or input) allows you to display errors after user interaction, improving UX.

questions.question: To create a dynamic list of input fields that users can add/remove, you can use __________ on an array and bind each input to an array element.
questions.explanation: `v-for` iterates over the array, creating a new input for each item, and `v-model` binds to the array element.

questions.question: HTML5 built‑in validation attributes like `required` and `pattern` are sufficient for all validation needs.
questions.explanation: HTML5 validation is basic and styling is limited. Complex validation (e.g., cross‑field checks) requires custom logic or libraries.

questions.question: Which library is the most popular for form validation in Vue?
questions.explanation: VeeValidate is the most widely used validation library for Vue, with extensive features and documentation.

questions.question: To make a form accessible, you should associate each input with a __________ using the `for` attribute.
questions.explanation: Properly associated `<label>` elements are crucial for screen reader users to understand form fields.

questions.question: The `aria-live` region can be used to announce dynamic validation errors to screen readers.
questions.explanation: `aria-live` tells screen readers to announce changes in the content, such as error messages.

questions.question: What is the difference between `v-model.lazy` and the default `v-model` behavior?
options: `.lazy` syncs after the `change` event instead of `input`
questions.explanation: `.lazy` updates the bound property only when the input loses focus (change event), reducing updates during typing.

questions.question: To focus the first input field when a component mounts, you can use a __________ and call `.focus()` in the `mounted` hook.
questions.explanation: A template ref allows direct access to the DOM element, enabling programmatic focus.

questions.question: You can combine validation libraries like VeeValidate with custom validation logic.
questions.explanation: Yes, VeeValidate allows custom rules and can also integrate with Yup for schema validation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `role="alert"` attribute on an error message container?
options: It styles the message as an alert
It tells screen readers to announce the message immediately
It prevents the message from being ignored by browsers
questions.explanation: `role="alert"` causes screen readers to announce the content immediately when it appears, which is ideal for error messages.

questions.question: To bind a checkbox to a boolean value, you use `v-model` without any modifiers. The bound property will be __________ when checked.
questions.explanation: For a single checkbox, `v-model` binds to a boolean: `true` when checked, `false` when unchecked.

questions.question: The `v-model.number` modifier works even if the input is of type `text`.
questions.explanation: Yes, `.number` attempts to parse the input value as a number regardless of input type.

questions.question: When using a custom component that supports multiple `v-model` bindings, how do you access the values?
options: They are merged into a single `modelValue` object
Each binding corresponds to a separate prop (e.g., `firstName`) and event (`update:firstName`)
They cannot be used with custom components
They must be passed as an array
questions.explanation: Each `v-model:prop` becomes a separate prop and a separate `update:prop` event.

questions.question: A validation library that allows defining a schema with `Yup` and integrates with Vue is __________.
questions.explanation: VeeValidate has built‑in integration with Yup for schema‑based validation.

questions.question: You should avoid using `placeholder` as a substitute for a `<label>` because it disappears when typing.
questions.explanation: Placeholders are not accessible and are not a replacement for proper labels; they also vanish after input.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to validate a form with fields that depend on each other (e.g., password and confirm password)?
options: Use separate computed properties for each field
Create a custom validator that checks both fields
Use a watcher to validate after changes
questions.explanation: You can use computed properties that reference both fields, or a custom validator in a library like VeeValidate. Watchers can also trigger validation.
